author: ai
text: The dispute over the Tigris and Euphrates involves Turkey, Iran, Syria and Iraq. Under a 1987 protocol, Turkey undertook to release an average flow of 500 cubic metres per second of the Euphrates at its border with Syria (1987). In January 1990, Turkey began filling the reservoir of the Atatürk Dam on the Euphrates. Under a 1990 agreement, Syria and Iraq share the Euphrates water entering Syria from Turkey, with Iraq's share set at 58% (1990). Turkey began filling the Ilısu Dam reservoir on the Tigris in July 2019. Türkiye and Iraq signed the Framework Agreement on Cooperation in the Field of Water Policy on 22 April 2024.
